sentences.text: This part reads chest pain type, resting blood pressure, fasting blood sugar, chest pain on exercise, ST depression, the ST segment and the thallium scan; it acts on 93 of 242 training patients, 76 of whom had heart disease, and for its typical patient takes the predicted risk from about 89% without it to above 99% with it.

Through it, ST depression on exercise raises the risk, and even more so with a reversible defect on the thallium scan, in an uneven way: for a typical patient from about 31% at 0 mm to about 74% at 2.8 mm with that defect, while without it the risk stays at about 31%.

For most patients with a downsloping ST segment, ST depression adds nothing until about 1.9 mm (between 0.3 and 3.0 mm for different patients), then raises the risk steadily, from about 10% to about 66% (the model has little data on this, n = 6 to 9), but for patients with non-anginal chest pain or chest pain on exercise it rises slowly at first, then faster.
